column4: Identical locked camera and wall of small puppet theater cells as the first reference (five columns, four rows). Every cell holds a small porcelain maid doll sitting with closed eyes, except that in the cell at the third column of the second row the doll has stood up and is stepping out: one white boot over the sill of the cell, her hand holding the cell's frame, her eyes open, stepping out across the frame toward the viewer. The other cells keep their dolls sitting, eyes closed. Same new doll as the second reference. No strings, no text.

Identical locked camera, cathedral nave, pews, statues and steps as the first reference, but now both tall doors have been swung wide open against the side walls, showing their inner faces with the ironwork. The whole doorway opening between the open doors, from the threshold up to the pointed arch, is one flat pure chroma green (#00B140) with nothing at all visible inside it. The floor and carpet inside the nave stay unchanged. No people, no text.

Full-body view of the same living librarian as in the references, seen from behind and the side, standing upright and looking back over her shoulder at the viewer with a gentle, steady expression, her face in three-quarter view. Her right arm is extended backwards and low, slightly out from her body, the hand held open with two fingers pinching the very end of a fine thread, wrist relaxed. Her left arm hangs at her side. She is a living human: natural skin, no ball joints, no wrist rings. Exactly two arms, two legs, two feet and five fingers per hand. The entire background is one flat pure chroma green (#00B140) with nothing else in it; clean closed outline, no thread drawn, no floor, no shadow, no text.
